meta.title: KaaroViewer: An Immersive Cognitive Interface
meta.subtitle: From 3D graph viewer to self-evolving intelligence platform

report_card.summary: kaaroViewer transforms text documents into multi-layered intelligence briefs and renders them as interactive 3D knowledge graphs. Its architecture runs from user-driven LLM encoding (explore pipeline or /visualize skill) through Three.js spatial rendering to a self-improving life system — health-check, Alone-Time loop, and Dream Loop — that autonomously monitors and corrects library quality without user intervention.

story.title: The Problem of Comprehension
story.narration: Modern intelligence analysis requires traversing dense webs of interconnected information. Linear documents flatten relationships, collapse causal chains, and bury structure in prose. Reading alone is insufficient. The problem is not the absence of data — it is the absence of spatial, navigable form for the data that exists.

story.title: The Rendering Bet
story.narration: kaaroViewer chose Three.js as its rendering engine — a cross-browser 3D JavaScript library that enables force-directed graph layout, animated node transitions, and WebXR immersion. The original architecture used A-Frame as a declarative WebXR wrapper, which has since been superseded by a direct Three.js canvas implementation for finer control over rendering and interaction.

story.title: The Intelligence Brief Standard
story.narration: The central innovation is not the renderer — it is the data model. A single source document encodes into seven simultaneous layers: meta, nodes, edges, story beats, insights, clusters, and a report card. Each layer is a different lens on the same subject. The validator enforces this structure: no entry reaches the library without passing schema checks, density thresholds, and cross-reference integrity.

story.title: Two Paths to Library
story.narration: Two routes produce intelligence briefs. The explore pipeline runs in-browser — a Gemini-powered LLM call that parses a topic into a draft brief in seconds. It is fast and exploratory, seeding the canvas for first contact with a subject. The /visualize Claude skill is deliberate and library-grade: three structured passes (nodes → edges → narrative) with explicit quality gates. Only /visualize produces entries that reach the permanent library.

story.title: Enrichment and the Completion Machine
story.narration: After initial encoding, the completion pipeline runs three enrichment passes: stub nodes for story beat references missing from the graph, Wikidata SPARQL lookups to attach real-world context (descriptions, images, linked entities), and edge stubs for implied relationships. The graph does not remain static once encoded — it is progressively enriched as context becomes available.

story.title: Paint, Memory, and Navigation
story.narration: Four canvas capabilities layer atop the renderer. The P-key triggers the paint system: Gemini reads the enriched context (current node, camera angle, active story beat) and generates a contextual image through one of four strategies — cinematic, documentary, abstract, or blueprint. The session manager persists explorations to IndexedDB so users return to their previous position. The brief controller drives slide-based narrative navigation across story beats.

story.title: The Eval Signal
story.narration: Users can evaluate any library entry via the L-key drawer. Rating and observations pre-fill a GitHub Issue tagged 'eval'. The health-check module polls these signals alongside validator exit codes and edge density to generate a machine-readable quality portrait of the library — the first time the system could observe its own degradation without a human audit.

story.title: The System Becomes Self-Aware
story.narration: The Alone-Time loop is a scheduled autonomous agent that reads the health report, selects the weakest library entry, re-encodes it via /visualize with explicit gap targeting, and commits only if both the validator and the full 168-test suite pass. Four runs have now completed — three degraded entries corrected to ok, one Dream Loop triggered and executed. The library improves without user instruction.

story.title: Beyond Reading
story.narration: The system has moved from a static viewer to a living knowledge platform. Documents do not just become graphs — they become entries in a library that monitors its own quality, surfaces its own gaps, and corrects them autonomously. The paradigm has shifted from reading reports to actively exploring a self-evolving knowledge landscape.

insights.title: The seven-layer brief standard enables simultaneous factual, narrative, and analytical reading modes that linear documents structurally cannot provide
insights.body: Nodes and edges create a queryable factual graph. Story beats impose a causal narrative arc. Insights extract declarative claims. Clusters provide spatial grouping. Report card condenses the whole into a scannable summary. None of these layers can substitute for another — together they make a document simultaneously readable, explorable, and machine-improvable.

insights.title: Scalability past 300 nodes degrades spatial comprehension without dynamic focus modes and aggressive clustering
insights.body: The 3D canvas advantage inverts at high node counts: a graph of 400+ undifferentiated nodes is harder to navigate than a flat document. The current architecture mitigates this through tier-based visual scaling (spine/primary/secondary/anchor) and cluster-based spatial grouping, but no automatic focus-zoom or semantic filtering exists yet. This is the primary surface area where the viewer's own limitations will compound as the library grows.

insights.title: The explore-visualize split preserves exploration velocity while preventing library quality degradation through structural separation of concerns
insights.body: Explore pipeline runs in seconds, seeds the canvas, and is intentionally draft quality. /visualize runs over minutes, enforces three structured passes, and is the only path to a permanent library entry. Keeping these paths separate prevents the natural pressure of fast prototyping from eroding the quality floor of the permanent record. The validator is the membrane between them.

insights.title: The self-observing life architecture positions kaaroViewer as a template for autonomous library-quality maintenance in any document-to-graph system
insights.body: The combination of health-check (mirror), Alone-Time loop (mutation engine), validator + test suite (immune system), and Dream Loop (meta-governance) forms a complete self-improvement cycle. Any system that encodes structured documents into a quality-gated library could adopt this architecture — the three components are generic: a health metric, a mutation agent, and a gate. The specific encoding domain (knowledge graphs, legal databases, product catalogs) is fungible.

insights.title: The same validator that blocks human encoding errors is the primary guardrail against LLM-generated graph corruption
insights.body: validate-library-json.py was designed to catch human mistakes during /visualize sessions. It turned out to be equally effective as an LLM mutation guard: in four Alone-Time runs, the gate caught every bad edge, blocked every invalid type, and never passed a semantically broken entry. This is the immune system hypothesis (H6) confirmed: the validator's domain-agnostic structural checks are sufficient to catch LLM output corruption without semantic review.

nodes.label: kaaroViewer
nodes.description: A browser-based knowledge graph explorer. Users type a topic; an LLM pipeline generates a structured intelligence brief (nodes, edges, narrative beats, insights, clusters); Three.js renders it as an interactive 3D graph. The platform now includes a self-improving library system (health-check + Alone-Time + Dream Loop).

nodes.label: Intelligence Brief
nodes.description: The core data model. A single JSON document encoding a source into seven simultaneous layers: meta, nodes, edges, story beats, insights, clusters, and report_card. Each layer is a different analytical lens. The format is the system's lingua franca — everything reads it and everything writes to it.

nodes.label: Three.js
nodes.description: The 3D rendering engine underpinning the canvas. Manages force-directed graph layout, animated node transitions, tier-scaled geometry, sentiment aura rings, and the P-key paint texture layer. Initially wrapped by A-Frame; now used directly for finer rendering control.

nodes.label: Explore Pipeline
nodes.description: The in-browser LLM pipeline. Takes a user topic, calls a registered LLM function (Gemini or BYOM via localStorage config), parses the response into a validated intelligence brief JSON, and renders it to the Three.js canvas. Produces draft-quality briefs for exploratory use only — not library-grade.

nodes.label: /visualize Skill
nodes.description: The Claude-driven library-grade encoding skill. Three-pass structure: nodes first, edges second, narrative third. Enforces quality gates (edge density ≥ 2.0, 7–12 beats, exactly 1 climax, 4–7 insights, validator exit 0). The only path to a permanent library entry.

nodes.label: Paint System
nodes.description: P-key triggered Gemini image synthesis. PaintContext assembles enriched context (current node, camera angle, active story beat, cluster), PaintStrategies select the render style (cinematic / documentary / abstract / blueprint), and the generated image is applied as a node texture in Three.js. Results are cached per node+strategy combination.

nodes.label: Eval Modal
nodes.description: UGC evaluation system. Library drawer (L key) → EVAL button → rating (1-5) + structured observations → pre-fills a GitHub Issue at karx/kaaroViewer with label 'eval'. The eval signal feeds the health-check module, closes the loop between user experience and autonomous quality improvement.

nodes.label: Health Check
nodes.description: The system's self-portrait. scripts/health-check.mjs runs the validator on all library entries, polls GitHub eval issues, and emits a structured JSON health report: ok/watch/degraded/critical status per entry, degradation scores, and ranked recommendations. The Alone-Time loop's primary input.

nodes.label: Alone-Time Loop
nodes.description: An autonomous scheduled self-improvement process. Six steps per run: INGEST health report + previous handoff → SELECT worst entry → MUTATE via /visualize with gap targeting → GATE (validator + tests) → COMMIT → HANDOFF document. Four runs completed as of 2026-06-07; library improved from 3 degraded to 0 degraded. Escalates to Dream Loop when the same unresolved signal appears 3 consecutive times.

nodes.label: Wikidata
nodes.description: The external knowledge graph used for entity enrichment. Queried via SPARQL endpoints during the completion pipeline to attach real-world descriptions, images, and linked entities to spine and primary nodes in every intelligence brief.

nodes.label: Data Complexity
nodes.description: The fundamental problem kaaroViewer addresses: modern intelligence analysis requires navigating dense webs of interconnected information that resist linear reading. Cause: information is relational, but most presentation formats are sequential.

nodes.label: Validator
nodes.description: validate-library-json.py — the system's immune system. Enforces VALID_TYPES, VALID_RELS, edge density, cross-reference integrity, story beat structure, and insight quality. Exit 0 = valid. Exit 1 = warnings. Exit 2 = blocking errors. Runs as a pre-commit hook and as the Alone-Time gate. Upgraded by the Dream Loop when new constraints are needed.

nodes.label: A-Frame
nodes.description: The original WebXR framework that wrapped Three.js in kaaroViewer's first architecture. Provided a declarative HTML component model for VR scene building. Superseded by a direct Three.js canvas implementation for finer rendering control, though its WebXR capability remains the model for immersive support.

nodes.label: Completion Pipeline
nodes.description: pipeline/completion.mjs — runs three enrichment passes after initial encoding: stub nodes for missing story beat references, Wikidata SPARQL enrichment (metrics, descriptions, thumbnails), and edge stubs for implied relationships. Bridges the gap between draft and production-quality briefs.

nodes.label: Session Manager
nodes.description: canvas/session-manager.mjs — saves and restores exploration state to IndexedDB. Users return to their previous camera position, active story beat, and loaded brief. Enables persistence across browser sessions without a backend.

nodes.label: Brief Controller
nodes.description: canvas/brief-controller.mjs — manages the active brief state machine and drives slide-based navigation across story beats. Each beat is a 'slide' that focuses the camera and highlights relevant nodes. The primary UX layer between the data model and the renderer.

nodes.label: Information Overload
nodes.description: The downstream consequence of data complexity: the state of being overwhelmed by volume and density of information beyond the capacity to process meaningfully. kaaroViewer's clustering, tier-scaling, and focus modes are designed to keep this at bay as library size grows.

nodes.label: Gemini API
nodes.description: Google's multimodal LLM. The default provider for both the explore pipeline (brief generation) and the paint system (image synthesis from graph context). Accessible via API key stored in localStorage. Users can substitute any LLM via window.kaaro.registerLLM().

nodes.label: Paint Context
nodes.description: canvas/paint-context.mjs — assembles the enriched context object that the paint system sends to Gemini: current node metadata, active story beat narration, camera position, cluster membership, and visible neighbor nodes. The quality of generated images depends directly on the richness of this context.

nodes.label: Paint Strategies
nodes.description: A strategy registry for image generation styles: cinematic (dramatic lighting, wide-angle establishing), documentary (factual, journalistic), abstract (conceptual, geometric), blueprint (technical diagram, engineering). Strategies are swappable and extensible. Each produces a fundamentally different visual interpretation of the same graph context.

nodes.label: SPARQL
nodes.description: The query language used to fetch entity data from Wikidata. The completion pipeline constructs SPARQL queries for each spine and primary node to retrieve labels, descriptions, images, and linked QIDs.

nodes.label: WebXR
nodes.description: The W3C standard for immersive web experiences. kaaroViewer's Three.js canvas can enter WebXR mode, making the knowledge graph navigable in VR headsets. A-Frame was the original WebXR integration layer; the direct Three.js implementation preserves this capability.
